content.text: I want to start work on SYS-586 next, but I think this goes wider. What's best practice when it comes to component versus page layout design? How much responsibility should rest with the page to lay out components - presumably the idea should be that components should be easily re-usable in different contexts as appropriate and also Storybook's involvement means the components need to be testable and snapshottable sensibly on their own.

Good context from SYS-586 — the ticket itself already surfaces the exact issue: wrapping `SignIn` in `<Paper>` at the *page* level broke because tests render pages without a `MantineProvider`, and had to be patched around rather than fixing the actual architecture.

My recommendation: split it by what the wrapper is *for*, not by convenience.

- **Container (width/measure)** is a page-layout concern — it's about how a page arranges its content on the screen, not what the component *is*. Pages should own it, ideally via `<Container size="sm">` etc. using Mantine's theme sizes instead of ad hoc `maw="35rem"` — that's literally what SYS-586 is asking for.
- **Paper/Card (chrome — elevation, border, background)** is usually part of a component's own visual identity, not something imposed by context. If a component looks "broken" without its Paper wrapper regardless of where it's placed, the Paper belongs *inside* the component, not bolted on at the page. That's why the SignIn/Paper test breakage was a smell: it meant a presentational detail of the component leaked into the page, forcing every consumer (including tests and Storybook) to know about a dependency that should've been internal.

The tradeoff: pushing chrome into components risks double-wrapping if a component is later composed inside another Paper/Card, and pages lose some flexibility to vary presentation per context. Mitigate that by making chrome conditional via a prop (e.g. `withBorder`/`padded` defaulting sensibly) rather than hardcoding it, and always render the component standalone in Storybook so double-wrapping is visually obvious immediately.

Practical test for each existing case: **can this component be dropped into a Storybook story or a `.vitest.spec.tsx` render with nothing but `MantineProvider` and still look/behave correctly?** If not, whatever's missing (Paper, Card, spacing) should move inside the component. Want me to survey the codebase for current `maw=` and page-level `<Paper>`/`<Card>` usages to scope how big SYS-586 actually is before you commit to it?

Yes. I guess that really I need to take SYS-584 together with this, since I'm almost certainly going the wrong way by not using Container for layout on the player profile page. Possibly I can get rid of any lingering use of container queries

content.text:
**Root cause found and fixed.** It wasn't related to today's SYS-584/586 work — it was a regression from yesterday's commit `297ab1c9` ("SYS-594 Standardise on dot notation for table subcomponents").

That commit changed several components from standalone imports (`TableTr`, `TableTd`, etc.) to Mantine's dot-notation (`Table.Tr`, `Table.Td`). That's safe in Client Components, but four of the affected files — `PlayerInfo`, `PlayerResults`, `PlayerPositions`, `PlayerArse` — are Server Components (no `'use client'`). Under this stack (Next.js 16 + Turbopack), Mantine's compound static properties (`Table.Tbody`, `Table.Tr`, etc.) don't survive the RSC server/client serialization boundary, so they resolved to `undefined` at render time — hence "Element type is invalid: undefined." Client Components like `Turnout`, `WinnersTable`, and `RecordsTable` were unaffected because they never cross that boundary.

I confirmed this by bisecting the actual component tree on a from-scratch dev server (cache cleared, fresh process) rather than guessing from stack traces, which were too generic to pinpoint anything.

**Fix:** reverted just those four files to the standalone named imports (`TableTbody`/`TableTr`/`TableTh`/`TableTd`), leaving the dot-notation standardization intact everywhere it's actually safe (Client Components). Verified clean on players 1, 2, 3, and 201 on a completely fresh dev server, and `typecheck`/`lint`/`knip`/full component+page test suites (683 + 236 tests) all still pass.

**Takeaway for future work:** Mantine's dot-notation compound components (`Table.Tr`, `Table.Th`, etc.) are only safe in Client Components in this codebase — Server Components should keep using the standalone named imports. Worth a note in CLAUDE.md if you want to prevent this recurring.

Thank you for the report!

To explain why this is the case: when a server component imports a client component, it receives a special client reference that the RSC runtime knows how to send to the browser. In other words, you aren't receiving the underlying export, it's only used to be passed to the client. 

This is described a bit here: https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client:
> When a server evaluated module imports values from a 'use client' module, the values must either be a React component or [supported serializable prop values](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#passing-props-from-server-to-client-components) to be passed to a Client Component. Any other use case will throw an exception

However, I think the error itself can be improved here. React actually has a special message for this case which should read something like:

> Error: Cannot access <module> on the server. You cannot dot into a client module from a server component. You can only pass the imported name through.

We will investigate why it's not being shown in this particular case.

content.text:
Yes — this is a known, confirmed issue in the Next.js RSC architecture, not something specific to Mantine or this codebase.

**`vercel/next.js#84961`** — "Compound components are throwing Error: Element type is invalid in next 15.5.5" — is essentially the exact same bug: a compound sub-component (`Tabs.Tab` in their repro, `Table.Tr` in ours) logs as `undefined` when accessed from a Server Component, but as a real function from inside the component's own client module. A Next.js maintainer confirmed the fix is making the accessing component `'use client'` and linked to the fuller explanation.

**`vercel/next.js#75192`** has the actual root-cause explanation from a Next.js team member (`ztanner`): when a Server Component imports a `'use client'` module, it only receives an opaque **client reference** for passing to the browser — not the real export — so you cannot "dot into" a sub-property of it (`Table.Tr`) from server code; you can only pass the named import straight through as a component. React has a dedicated, clearer error for this ("Cannot access `<module>` on the server...") but Next.js isn't consistently surfacing it, which is why we saw the generic "Element type is invalid: undefined" instead — that gap is acknowledged but still open, and a commenter notes there are "numerous issues on the topic" (referencing `#76000`).

So: not a bug in Mantine's `Table` itself, and not fixable via a Mantine or Next.js update — it's an inherent constraint of the current RSC model. The correct pattern (matching what we just restored) is what Mantine's own docs and the linked writeup recommend: Server Components must use the standalone named exports (`TableTr`, `TableTd`, etc.), reserving the dot-notation (`Table.Tr`) for Client Components only.

Sources:
- [Compound components are throwing Error: Element type is invalid in next 15.5.5 (#84961)](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/84961)
- [RSC dot-notation explanation (#75192)](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/75192)
- [Multipart namespace components: addressing RSC and dot-notation issues](https://ivicabatinic.from.hr/posts/multipart-namespace-components-addressing-rsc-and-dot-notation-issues)

Before doing the bulk conversion, I hit one genuine blocker worth flagging: `@mantine/tiptap`'s `RichTextEditorToolbar` (used as `RichTextEditor.Toolbar` in `RichTextMailBody.tsx` and `SendEmailForm.tsx`) has **no public standalone export** — its package `exports` map only exposes the package root, and the toolbar component only exists as a static property on `RichTextEditor`. Every other dot-notation usage in the codebase (Table, AppShell, Popover, ScrollArea, Progress, Menu, and all the other RichTextEditor controls) does have a real standalone named export I can switch to.

57	## Architecture & Layers
58	
59	- **Pages:** `src/app/footy/**` — Next.js App Router feature pages
60	- **API routes:** `src/app/api/**` — Next.js route handlers; importable via `api/*` alias
61	- **Server actions:** `src/actions/` — thin `"use server"` wrappers: auth guard + call core + revalidate + broadcast; mutations only; injected into components as required props
62	- **Action cores:** `src/lib/core/` — pure business logic called by server actions; injectable deps for testing; no Next.js boundary concerns
63	- **Services:** `src/services/` — all Prisma queries live here exclusively, one service per model
64	- **Library:** `src/lib/` — utilities, auth, config, email, Azure, dates, URLs, observability
65	- **Types:** `src/types/` — custom TypeScript types and Zod schema extensions
66	
67	**Domain ontology:** [`docs/ontology.yaml`](docs/ontology.yaml) — the meaning layer on top of `prisma/schema.prisma`: what each entity represents, how they relate, controlled vocabularies, business workflows (invitations, picker, results, money), and invariants the code enforces that the schema doesn't. Consult it before making non-trivial changes to domain logic (game days, outcomes, picker, ratings, tables, transactions) — read `prisma/schema.prisma` for structure and this file for meaning. While changes to the ontology are possible they are likley to be rare and each should be considered very carefully: the business logic and the ontology should always be kept in sync.
68	
69	**Data flow rule:** Components call services (read) or server actions (write). Never write direct Prisma calls in API routes, pages, or components — refactor into a service method. If you filter/sort service results in calling code, move that logic into the service.
70	
71	## Key Conventions
72	
73	### Dependencies
74	
75	- `@types/d3` is listed in `devDependencies` and `ignoreDependencies` in `knip.json` even though no code imports from `d3` directly. It is kept because it pulls in all the individual `@types/d3-*` sub-packages (e.g. `@types/d3-array`, `@types/d3-axis`) as transitive npm dependencies — removing it silently removes all those type declarations.
76	
77	### Imports
78	
79	- **Always** use `@/` alias instead of `../../` relative imports
80	- Same-directory `./` imports are acceptable
81	- Always use single quotes for import paths
82	- Prepend all backend-only modules with `import 'server-only';`
83	- All imports from any `@mantine/*` package must be written multi-line, one specifier per line with a trailing comma, regardless of specifier count or line length (this applies even to a single-specifier import, e.g. `import {\n    Table,\n} from '@mantine/core';`)
84	
85	### Services Pattern
86	
87	```ts
88	import 'server-only';
89	import debug from 'debug';
90	import prisma from 'prisma/prisma';
91	import { SomeModelWhereUniqueInputObjectSchema } from 'prisma/zod/schemas';
92	import z from 'zod';
93	
94	const extendedFields = { /* extra validation */ };
95	export const SomeModelCreateStrictSchema = /* extend generated create schema */;
96	const log = debug('footy:api');
97	
98	export class SomeModelService {
99	  async get(id: number) {
100	    const where = SomeModelWhereUniqueInputObjectSchema.parse({ id });
101	    return prisma.someModel.findUnique({ where });
102	  }
103	}
104	```
105	
106	- Validate all inputs with Zod before calling Prisma (`WhereUnique`, `WhereInput`, or custom strict schema)
107	- Return `null` for "not found"; throw only on unexpected failures
108	- Use `debug('footy:api')` for logging; never `console.log`
109	- Use `lib/config.ts` for numeric thresholds instead of hardcoding
110	
111	### Prisma / Database
112	
113	- Prisma client singleton: `prisma/prisma.ts` — never instantiate another client
114	- Generated files in `prisma/generated/` and `prisma/zod/` — extend, never modify
115	- Use `z.email()` not `z.string().email()` (Zod deprecation)
116	- Never create migration files manually — use `npm run migrate`
117	- Better Auth tables (`user`, `account`, `session`, `verification`) — never modify directly via Prisma; use Better Auth APIs
118	
119	### UI & Forms
120	
121	- Use Mantine components and hooks everywhere; avoid native HTML/CSS unless no Mantine equivalent exists. Never fall back to raw `<div>`, `<section>`, `<article>` etc. just to attach ARIA attributes — use Mantine's polymorphic `component` prop (e.g. `<Card component="section">`) or `role`/`aria-*` props on the Mantine element instead
122	- Prefer Mantine style props (`bd`, `bg`, `c`, `w`, `h`, `m*`, `p*`, etc.) over the `style` prop or a CSS file/module. Only fall back to raw CSS/inline `style` when no Mantine style prop covers the property needed — CSS is the escape hatch, not the default
123	- **Always** use Mantine `useForm` for form state — never write bespoke form handlers
124	- Use `@tabler/icons-react` for icons
125	- Notifications: use Mantine `notifications` with `autoClose` from `lib/config.ts`
126	- British English for all copy and comments
127	
128	### Testing
129	
130	- Test files: `*.vitest.spec.ts(x)` placed next to the file they test — never in a `__tests__/` subdirectory
131	- Mocks: `__mocks__/` as sibling to the target code
132	- Use accessible selectors (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`, `getByText`) over `data-testid`
133	- Do not rely on Mantine internals in tests (for example generated class names, internal DOM wrappers, or implementation-specific structure). Prefer selectors and assertions that reflect real user interactions and visible behaviour.
134	- Prefer the generic overload (`getByRole<HTMLInputElement>(…)`) over a type assertion (`as HTMLInputElement`) when narrowing query results — ESLint strips assertions but preserves generics
135	- Don't test generated Zod schemas directly — test service method behaviour and validation
136	- E2E tests: `e2e/*.spec.ts`, must be fully parallel-safe
137	
138	### Comments & JSDoc
139	
140	- Default to no comments; only add one when the WHY is non-obvious
141	- When changing a function that has a JSDoc block, update the entire block in the same edit — description, `@param`, `@returns`, `@throws`, and any other tags must all accurately reflect the new implementation
142	
143	### Live updates (revalidation & SSE)
144	
145	Every server action that mutates data must, before returning:
146	
147	1. Call `revalidatePath(…)` for every Next.js route that renders the affected data.
148	2. Call `broadcast(channel)` (or `broadcast([ch1, ch2])` for multiple) from `@/lib/events` with the relevant `FootyChannel` value(s) — so connected clients refresh without polling.
149	
150	Every page that displays data that can be mutated by a server action must render `<AutoRefresh channels={…} />` (from `@/components/AutoRefresh/AutoRefresh`) with the matching channel(s). Pass an array when the page depends on more than one channel — never render multiple `<AutoRefresh>` elements.
151	
152	`FootyChannel` values live in `src/types/FootyChannel.ts`; add a new entry there if the new feature needs its own channel.
153	
154	### Observability
155	
156	- Sentry: configured via `instrumentation.ts` / `instrumentation-client.ts` and `next.config.mjs`
157	- Preserve `tunnelRoute: '/monitoring'` and middleware matcher exclusions when editing middleware
158	
159	## Tech Stack
160	
161	| Layer | Technology |
162	| --- | --- |
163	| Framework | Next.js (App Router) + React |
164	| Database | MariaDB via Prisma ORM |
165	| UI | Mantine |
166	| Auth | Better Auth (Google, Microsoft OAuth + email) |
167	| Testing | Vitest + Playwright + Storybook |
168	| API mocking | MSW |
169	| Validation | Zod (with Prisma-generated schemas) |
170	| Monitoring | Sentry |
171	| Storage | Azure Blob Storage |
172	| Email | Nodemailer via Microsoft Graph |
173	| Containers | Docker Compose (MariaDB + Mailpit) |
174	| Secrets | 1Password (`op run`) |
